title: Tripo, Higgsfield or ComfyUI?
author: Beginning-Sign1916
selftext: So I have reach the stage where I am starting to get my 3D models for my game and I am talking about like characters, props, environment so what’s the best tool you guys have been using and the pros and cons to it

comments.author: ChadSexman
comments.body:
Meshy for easy “game ready” models, if you can afford it.

Local models and blender MCP if you can not.

comments.author: Ukatyushas
comments.body:
For a fidelity similar to Company of Heroes 2 and characters, I have been having a lot of success with using Higgsfield to generate the reference art, which is front view, side profile view and back view in A Pose. I typically use Nano Banana Pro 16:9 at 2K resolution.

Once I have the reference I separate it into 3 images for each view. I then use those images in tripo with the multi-view input using the new P2.0 in smart topology with quads. I typically target 5K faces for a human with simple clothes. 10K if they have a lot of accessories on top of the clothes. After I am happy with the model in tripo I texture it there then export as fbx for blender.

I then import into blender to fix any issues such as scaling or holes. I then rig with Auto-rig Pro.

Target engine is godot.

The largest inefficiency I think is back and forth between changing mesh and texturing. But I think this can be mostly alleviated if you have an intelligent framework for what is part of one mesh vs separate and attached. That depends on your game.

comments.author: ichivictus
comments.body: I just use Opus 5.5 with blender mcp. I haven't found a need to spend more money on Tripo or another service like it.

replies.author: Beginning-Sign1916
replies.body: Do you mind sharing more? I was using Opus 5.5 then I switch to Sonnet 5.5 and now Terra 6.1 and I gotta say Opus 5.5 was more on the high side of tokens but in terms of quality in blender Sonnet 5.5 and Terra 6.1 seems better and cost less

replies.author: ichivictus
replies.body:
Yeah, I haven't messed with the lower models for blender work. Opus 5.5 does a great job for me when I either give it reference images or it already knows the style of the project I am working on. I have it render the results and I have it iterate several times till I am happy. Then I have it import to Unity and go from there. I haven't had any problems with it but I guess it depends on what it is you are working on.

  
For characters, I am working on a game with anime characters. So I purchased some on [booth.pm](http://booth.pm) and customize to my liking with opus. It costs less and is quicker to use assets like that than to spend the tokens probably.

comments.author: BeingComfortablyDumb
comments.body:
ComfyUI most cost efficient and customiseable. There's a learning curve but once you figure it out. Sky is the limit. Open Source is your God. 

Tripo if you want to just mostly automate and review. 

I honestly dont understand why Higgsfield is even this list. It's just a comfyUI wrapper, difference being they have their own workflow that makes it easy and fast but costly af.

comments.author: FragmentedHeap
comments.body:
ComyUI is strong if you have the hardware, ComfyUI has an MCP you can use in Claude, that coupled with the Blender MCP, there's really nothing you can't do.

If you have a 3090 or better, 24+ gb vram, you can run Pixal 3d, Hi3d, nvidias new animate model, and much much much more, entire on local hardware.

You can also run MiniMax h3 and it has a compase lora that can orbit a character in the video and you can pull reference images from that and then use that for pixel 3d meshes and refine them with hi3d, and so on.

There's a plethora of things you can do with comfyui + blender, especially if you pay for blender plugins like Meta Humans etc etc.
